entries.title: Instructional Scores for Reading Rooms (Score Sheet No. 4)
entries.titleZh: 阅览室指令乐谱（第4号乐谱）
entries.medium: Printed facsimile booklet, A4, 16 pages, thread sewn
entries.shortDescription: A multi-page instructional score and performance facsimile for silent reading rooms, published in edition with selectable text and downloadable PDF.
entries.fullText:
A published multi-page score containing typographic choreographies, silent reading rules, and transcription constraints for public libraries.
    
Designed to be opened upon communal library desks. Readers follow pacing notations, intervals of quiet turning, and ink depletion markings.

blocks.content:
“Instructional Scores for Reading Rooms (Score Sheet No. 4)” compiles sixteen instructional protocols enacted across public reading rooms.
        
Rather than conventional musical notation, the score uses typographic line lengths, caesura gaps, and margins to pace the reader's breath and page turnover.

Use the embedded PDF reader below to page through the facsimile with selectable text, zoom into fine typographic details, or download the original PDF file.

blocks.title: Instructional Scores for Reading Rooms (Score Sheet No. 4) — PDF Facsimile
blocks.description: Archival PDF facsimile (14 pages). Typeset score sheet with selectable text, paired spread views, zoom, and progress indicator.

blocks.content:
Performance parameters:
- To be read in silent public libraries without audio amplification.
- Readers may enact Score No. 4 individually or in pairs across facing tables.
- Consult related publication [[part-time-book-club-zine]] and research project [[ss-between-books-and-libraries]].

entries.title: Part Time Book Club: Issue 01 (Reading Transcript Zine)
entries.titleZh: 兼职读书会 第一期：阅读室听记
entries.medium: Risograph printed zine, black soy ink on 80gsm book paper, 6 pages
entries.shortDescription: A 6-page transcribed reading transcript zine documenting the first collective reading session of the Part Time Book Club, presented with single and paired-spread viewing.
entries.fullText: Issue 01 of the Part Time Book Club zine collects transcriptions, reading protocols, and reader marginalia from the October 2022 reading session in Shanghai.

blocks.content:
The Part Time Book Club zine is printed in small batches on risograph duplicators and distributed directly to session attendees.
        
Issue 01 establishes the foundational methodology of [[part-time-book-club]]: reading silently together, slowing transcription speed to match the hand, and sharing an unpressured collective environment.

Below is the complete 6-page document reader. On desktop, you can switch between **Single Page** and **Paired Page (Spread)** viewing; on mobile devices, it automatically defaults to a clean single-page presentation.

entries.title: 述书: Facsimile of Library Inscriptions (Pre-composed Spreads)
entries.titleZh: 述书：图书馆题记影印（整版跨页）
entries.medium: Exposed thread binding, archival offset reproduction on warm matte paper
entries.shortDescription: A volume of archival book spread scans documenting marginal inscriptions across independent libraries, presented in their original pre-composed two-page spreads without gutter cropping.
entries.fullText: Archival facsimile volume containing two-page spread plates of annotated volumes and reader inscriptions.

blocks.content:
When documenting bound volumes, splitting facing pages into isolated vertical slices damages the spatial relationship between marginal notes and facing texts.
        
In this volume, each scan represents an **already-composed two-page spread** (open folio). The document reader displays each spread intact, allowing you to pan, zoom, and inspect marginal inscriptions across the central gutter.

Spread 03 (pp. 6–7): Reader notation map tracking four distinct hands in the margin.
Spread 04 (pp. 8–9): Library stamp registry and printer's colophon.

blocks.description: Four pre-composed archival spreads (pp. 2–9). Proportions are strictly preserved to maintain legibility of handwritten annotations.

entries.shortDescription: A three-part moving image suite examining handwriting duration, library navigation, and transcription rhythm across YouTube, Vimeo, and Google Drive video providers.

blocks.content:

Each video is displayed in a responsive 16:9 container with zero autoplay, fallback external links, and optional captions and credits. For Google Drive files, clear guidance is provided regarding permissions.

entries.fullText:
A continuing series of working notes, marginalia, and transcribed fragments examining the hand as a recording device.

Looking at how [[copying]] transforms involuntary motor habit into conscious gesture. Rather than preparing for a singular completed object, these pages register transcription rhythm, line pauses, and the ink's gradual depletion.

entries.title: thank you for your time
entries.shortDescription: A work considering spent attention, conversational formula, and the temporal transactions of social exchange.
entries.fullText:
Taking the ubiquitous closing phrase of institutional correspondence and daily courtesy—"thank you for your time"—as both subject and boundary.

Investigates duration, interpersonal indebtedness, and the formal protocols of polite departure. Closely dialogues with [[scores]] and structured encounters.

*Placeholder entry: Specific medium, installation form, and documentation to be confirmed by Hong Shu-ying.*

entries.title: 模仿要像：如歌
entries.shortDescription: An inquiry into pedagogical repetition, musical cadence (cantabile), and the fidelity demanded by imitation.
entries.fullText:
Exploring the pedagogical mandate "模仿要像" (to imitate faithfully / to look exactly like the model) paired with the musical directive "如歌" (cantabile / song-like, expressive and flowing).

Considers the tension between mechanical precision and affective expression in classical training, bodily discipline, and voice. Directly connected to [[copying]] and graphic [[scores]].

entries.title: 述书 / SS: between books & libraries
entries.medium: Research, publishing, reading sessions, library interventions
entries.shortDescription: A long-term project traversing books, public and independent libraries, reader communities, personal collections, and reading sessions.
entries.fullText:
“述书 / SS: between books & libraries” is an ongoing framework within Hong Shu-ying's practice. 

The name draws upon *Shu Shu* (述书)—recounting, narrating, or commenting on books—while positioning the work in the interval between books as bound objects and libraries as collective spatial institutions.

It encompasses:
- **Books**: Printed matter, artists' publications, annotated volumes, and marginalia.
- **Libraries**: Independent archives, institutional collections, public reading rooms, and personal shelves.
- **People & Conversations**: Readers, custodians, transcribers, and librarians.
- **Programmes**: Reading groups, including the [[part-time-book-club]], translation circles, and collective reading aloud.

Rather than remaining an isolated project, SS branches into works, notes on [[copying]], and transcribed [[script-notes]].

entries.title: Part Time Book Club
entries.medium: Collective reading sessions, shared marginalia, reading lists
entries.shortDescription: Informal, periodic gatherings around reading, printed matter, and shared marginalia, developed within 述书 / SS.
entries.fullText:
An informal reading collective convened on a "part-time" basis, resisting the professionalization of reading and creating non-coercive spaces for close study.

Participants bring books, unread essays, or fragments to read alongside one another. The club explores reading as a physical, shared occupation rather than an isolated intellectual test.

Organized as part of [[ss-between-books-and-libraries]] and informed by practices of [[scores]] and collective recitation.

*Note for artist review: Dates, frequency, and meeting locations kept open as placeholders.*

entries.title: scores
entries.shortDescription: Instructional diagrams, reading sequences, and choreographies for voice, eyes, or hand.
entries.fullText:
The score (谱, pu) functions in this practice not merely as musical notation, but as an open script for action, observation, and time-keeping.

A score can be:
- A typographic layout directing the eye's wandering speed
- An invitation for two strangers to share silence
- A sequence of physical constraints for transcription

Entries engaging with scores include [[thank-you-for-your-time]], [[mofang-yaoxiang-ruge]], and [[instructional-scores-pdf]].

entries.title: copying
entries.shortDescription: Copying as an embodied method of close looking, critical proximity, and cognitive transcription rather than mechanical reproduction.
entries.fullText:
Copying (临摹 linmo / 抄录 chaolu) is considered here as an active epistemic tool.

By tracing another's words, strokes, or cadence, the copyist inhabits the original text from the inside. The divergence—the involuntary tremble, the slight misreading, the fatigue of the wrist—reveals the boundary between the original and the self.

Connects deeply to [[mofang-yaoxiang-ruge]], [[script-notes]], and the archival ethos of [[ss-between-books-and-libraries]].

about.title: About
about.biography:
Hong Shu-ying 方舒颖’s practice works across text, paper studies, transcription, instructional scores, and library interventions. Her work is situated within the daily rhythms of reading, handwriting, repetition, and the relational protocols of attention.

Rather than presenting a closed catalogue of finished monuments, this site functions as an evolving index. Developing ideas, found images, and working notes are catalogued alongside completed works, allowing connections between conceptual terms (such as [title]copying[/title] or [title]scores[/title]) and collective projects (such as 述书 / SS: between books & libraries and the Part Time Book Club) to remain visible and active.
